description: REQ-004(b) (behavioral-spec.md:257-259) requires 'prevent runtime/anicca-daemon.sh's ensure_brain function ... from starting franklin proxy --port 8403 ... for INSTANCE=franklin' but never specifies what ensure_brain's franklin branch SHOULD do instead. The real anicca-daemon.sh (read on disk, /Users/operator/anicca/runtime/anicca-daemon.sh) has TWO structurally separate branches of a single 'if [ "$INSTANCE" = "franklin" ]; then ... else ... fi' block (lines 54-100): the franklin branch (lines 54-75) defines its OWN local ensure_brain() that spawns `franklin proxy`; the non-franklin/else branch (lines 76-100) defines a DIFFERENT local ensure_brain() (lines 82-95) that spawns `clawrouter` using a wallet key resolved by FIRST grepping the SHARED, cross-instance file `$HOME/.openclaw/.env` for BLOCKRUN_WALLET_KEY (line 88: `grep -E '^BLOCKRUN_WALLET_KEY=' "$HOME/.openclaw/.env"`), falling back only then to `resolve-identity.mjs evm` (line 92). That grep is UNCONDITIONAL on ANICCA_HOME -- it is not gated per-instance the way resolve-identity.mjs's own resolveEvmPrivateKey/resolveSolanaSecret are (verified: skills/earn/lib/resolve-identity.mjs:63-87). REQ-004(b)'s silence on what replaces the removed franklin-branch spawn leaves at least two materially different, spec-compliant implementations: (a) make franklin's ensure_brain a no-op/empty function (safe: relies on the already-running shared ClawRouter, per behavioral-spec.md's own Context claim that it is 'already-running' at spec-writing time -- but says nothing about what happens on a cold boot where NO instance has started ClawRouter yet, so franklin's daemon would then spin forever waiting on port 8402 with no code path to bring it up); or (b) collapse/merge the if/else so franklin's daemon falls into the SAME ensure_brain as the non-franklin branch, in which case Franklin's OWN daemon process would read $HOME/.openclaw/.env (a DIFFERENT instance's, i.e. the OpenClaw/anicca-a3cdd4 automaton's, wallet-key file) to spawn a ClawRouter process, and REQ-005 (behavioral-spec.md:331-354) -- 'SHALL NOT scan, read, or derive an address/balance from any other dot-directory's wallet/session file under any circumstance' -- and PROP-007 (verification-architecture.md:72, a Tier-2 money-safety invariant) do not cover this code path at all, since PROP-007/resolve-identity.test.mjs only test resolve-identity.mjs's own functions in isolation, never anicca-daemon.sh's ensure_brain wiring. Neither REQ-004 nor REQ-005 nor any PROP-0xx entry states which of (a)/(b) is required, or that a franklin-branch ensure_brain replacement must never read $HOME/.openclaw/.env or any other instance's wallet file. This is exactly the class of unspecified behavior this feature exists to close (the spec's own cited 'Efpap5 incident' precedent), left open by omission in the one place (daemon startup wiring, not library-level identity resolution) that this feature's own tests do not reach.

evidence.snippet: (b) prevent `runtime/anicca-daemon.sh`'s `ensure_brain` function (currently lines 53-75) from starting `franklin proxy --port 8403 --model nvidia/llama-4-maverick --no-fallback` for `INSTANCE=franklin`; AND

crossCheckedAgainst.note: confirmed live: two independent ensure_brain() closures, one per INSTANCE branch; non-franklin's spawns clawrouter using a cross-instance $HOME/.openclaw/.env grep at line 88, unconditional on ANICCA_HOME
the actual per-instance-gated resolver this feature relies on for REQ-005 -- not reached by anicca-daemon.sh's own inline $HOME/.openclaw/.env grep fallback path
